final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced

**Expected:** `WalkParallel::run()` does not hang when a visitor panics; the panic ("oops!") propagates to the caller, so the reporter's `#[should_panic(expected = "oops!")]` test passes.

**Actual:** The visitor panic prints `oops!`, then the test never finishes. The process stays up with all 41 threads alive (the 40 workers spinning or sleeping in the wait loop of `Worker::get_work`) until `timeout` kills it.

**Trigger:** The reporter's test: a temp dir with one file, `WalkBuilder::new(..).threads(40).build_parallel().run(|| Box::new(|_| panic!("oops!")))`. I did not try other thread counts.

**Run** (from the repo root, exit 124 from `timeout` while the bug is present):
```
cd crates/ignore && cargo test --offline --lib --no-run && TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout -k 2 20 cargo test --offline --lib -- panic_in_parallel
```
The same command is in `/work/runs/bd75270ed7/out/run_command.txt`. A healthy run finishes in about 0.1s, so 20s is generous. It uses a fresh `TMPDIR` on purpose. The shared `/tmp/rust-ignore/` already held directories 0..99, so the crate's test `TempDir` failed with "failed to create temp dir after 100 tries". That is a setup collision, not this bug. Killed hung runs also leave their directory behind, which caused the same collision in my own early runs.

**Passes when:** With a throwaway patch (since reverted), the same test passed 100/100 in about 0.1s each. The patch did four things:
- Wrapped `Worker::run` in `catch_unwind`.
- On a panic, set `quit_now`, pushed a `Quit` message and re-raised the panic.
- Added an `is_quit_now()` check inside the inner wait loop of `get_work`.
- Made `visit` resume the first worker panic payload instead of `join().unwrap()`.

Setting `quit_now` alone, without the inner-loop check, still hung. That matches the reporter's note that their first attempt didn't fully fix it.

**Reliability:** 100/100 runs hung on the unmodified tree (2s limit per run, fresh `TMPDIR` each time). Plain `cargo test` in `crates/ignore` also hangs, with `panic_in_parallel` never completing. The report describes the hang as occasional. Here it was every time.

**Likely cause:** The panicking worker never decrements `active_workers`, so the others never see "all done". They sit in the `get_work` wait loop, which only wakes on a `Quit` message and never checks `quit_now`.

**Artifacts:** I added the reporter's `panic_in_parallel` test to `crates/ignore/src/walk.rs`. It is the only change. No production code was changed.

One caveat on the check: it follows the reporter's test, so it requires the original "oops!" payload to come out of `run()`. A fix that propagates the panic with a different message would fail it.
run_command: cd crates/ignore && cargo test --offline --lib --no-run && TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d) timeout -k 2 20 cargo test --offline --lib -- panic_in_parallel
